requirement.description: 52 UD Physics units are required, distributed as follows

sections.notes: A grade of C- or above is required in order to continue the sequence of upper division courses.

narrative: For those students who have not completed AP calculus BC with a score of 5, Physics 8 is strongly recommended before attempting any other physics course.

MAJOR REGULATIONS
PREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Not allowed for any major course (Prep or UD major), including courses applied to the major from other departments.
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS…………………………………...With the approval of each department chairperson, up to a total of 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

nodes.title: Basic Astronomy
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: A survey of the development of astronomy with an emphasis on understanding the observable properties of the solar system, the sun and other stars, our own and other galaxies, and the entire universe. Topics of current interest will be discussed as time permits.

nodes.title: History of the Universe
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Astronomy 1.
nodes.description: Content will vary with the professor and student interests. Course has included modern extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, quasars, active galactic nuclei, dark matter, gravitational lenses, the early universe, the origins of life, and the possibility of extraterrestrial intelligence.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory).

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent Mathematics 3A course.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2A or CHEM 1A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Thermodynamics (first and second law), electrochemistry, chemical kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and chemical bonding.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory). First quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: Principles of Physical Geology
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: Introduction to the science of the Earth; properties and processes of its surface and interior, including plate tectonics, volcanism, earthquakes, glaciation, mountain building, formation of rocks, minerals, and the structural basis of landforms. Lab and lecture each offering. There can be an additional 1 day local field trip.

nodes.title: Giant Earthquakes
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Study of the character and causes of large earthquakes, the hazards they pose, and how society can prepare for and mitigate their impacts. Historical case studies will illuminate why their slip characteristics and destructive effects vary so widely.

nodes.title: Volcanoes and Humans
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: An introduction to volcanism and its consequences. Origins and physical processes of volcanism; the natural benefits of volcanoes; volcanic hazards and disasters; volcanoes in human history, society, and culture; volcanoes and climate; volcano monitoring and hazard mitigation.

nodes.title: Geological Catastrophes
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: Course deals with geologic catastrophes, e.g., earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, and landslides. Students will learn the basic physical causes of these naturally occurring events and discuss the consequences.

nodes.title: CalTeach, Elementary Mathematics Education
nodes.description: Introduction to learning and teaching mathematics in grades K-8. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

nodes.title: CalTeach, Elementary Science Education
nodes.description: Introduction to learning and teaching science in grades K-8. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

nodes.title: CalTeach, Secondary Mathematics Education
nodes.description: Introduction to learning and teaching mathematics in grades 7-12. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

nodes.title: CalTeach, Secondary Science Education
nodes.description: Introduction to learning and teaching science in grade 7-12. The course requires attending a weekly on-campus seminar and participating in 15 hours of field placement in a local school.

nodes.title: Teaching and Teachers
nodes.description: Provides a basic foundation for understanding both (a) the nature of teaching as a specialized human activity (as distinct from other human activities) and (b) the organization and conduct of teaching in contemporary U.S. schools.

groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math 2 Series
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math 2 Series
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math 3 Series
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Math 3 Series
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

nodes.title: Differential Equations
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.

nodes.title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Vector Calculus
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.

nodes.title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Vector Calculus
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

nodes.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
nodes.description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.

nodes.title: Concepts of Biology
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.description: Introduction to the science of life; cells, genetics, metabolism, molecular biology, physiology, natural selection, evolution, ecosystems; current news and controversial topics in biology.

nodes.title: Statics
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B, or Math 3B, or AP Calculus AB with a score of 5, or AP Calculus BC with a score of 3 or better; and Physics 7A, or Physics 1

items.text: AP Calculus AB with a score of 5

nodes.description: Introduction to applied mechanics. Forces, moments, couples, and resultants; vector algebra; construction of free body diagrams; equilibrium in 2- and 3-dimensions; analysis of frames, machines, trusses and beams; distributed forces; friction.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Dynamical Systems
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B and ME 16
nodes.description: Equations of Motion for Mechanical, Electrical, Heat, Fluid, and Control Systems. Block diagram algebra and interconnections. Laplace transform. Transfer functions and dynamic stability. First and second order systems. Frequency response. Introduction to mechanical vibrations and feedback control design.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Vibrations
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Topics relating to vibration in mechanical systems; exact and approximate methods of analysis, matrix methods, generalized coordinates and Lagrange's equations, applications of systems. Basic feedback systems and controlled dynamic behavior.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

items.text: AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 4 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Vectors, velocity, acceleration. Newton's laws. Work and energy. Linear momentum. Gravity. Static equilibrium. Rotational motion. Angular momentum.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Oscillatory motion. Vibrations, waves, sound. Fluids. Electrostatics and DC circuits. Magnetism and magnetic forces. Induction and Faraday's law. AC circuits. If time permits: Heat and thermodynamics.

nodes.title: Introductory Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Electromagnetic waves. Geometric optics, optical instruments. Interference and diffraction. Quantum theory of the atom. Nuclear physics. If time permits: Special relativity, elementary particle physics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Kinematics in 3D, Newton’s Laws, Energy, Momentum and Collisions, Rotation, Statics and Equilibrium

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Gravity, Periodic Motion and Oscillations, Mechanical Waves and Sound, Coulomb’s Law, Electric Field and Gauss’s Law, Electric Potential, DC circuits

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7B with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Magnetic Forces and Field, Induction, Inductance and AC circuits, Maxwell’s equations and E/M waves, Geometric and Physical Optics

nodes.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
nodes.description: Single variable functions, derivatives and integrals with applications to kinematics. Taylor series. Introduction to ordinary differential equations and Newtons second law as an ODE. Vectors and scalars with physics applications. Dot and cross products. Matrices and determinants. Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.

nodes.title: Honors Introduction to Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Experimental Phyics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 or 23 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Covers the essence of experimental research. Students study three different systems experimentally, and write short Physical Review style articles about the results. Students are responsible for deciding what to measure, how to analyze data, what conclusions can be reached, etc.

nodes.title: Honors Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Experimental Phyics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 4 or 24 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Computer control of experiments. Students learn LabView, and use it to measure and generate analog signals using a data acquisition card and a personal computer. Students ultimately use their computers to measure and control the temperature of a copper rod.

nodes.title: Honors Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Experimental Phyics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Experimental Phyics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 29 and Physics 23 (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation. Basic good practices in note-taking, data collection, data visualization, error estimation, error propagation, curve fitting, and drawing conclusions, all exercised in the context of phenomena from mechanics and electronics.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Experimental Phyics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 20AL and Physics 24 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, continued. Basics of image analysis, technical drawing, additive manufacturing, oscilloscope use, searching and digesting scientific literature, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL in the context of electromagnetic and optical phenomena.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Experimental Phyics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 20BL and Physics 25 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, with an emphasis on Scientific Communication and Experimental Design. Searching the scientific literature, reading a scientific paper, proposing and executing a measurement, and formally reporting on a measurement in writing, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL and 20BL in the context of modern physics phenomena.

nodes.title: General Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A/3A and Mathematics 2B/3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam score of 5.
nodes.description: Classical mechanics, kinematics, vectors, Newtons laws, work and energy, conservation laws, rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: General Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 21 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Rotational dynamics, fluid mechanics, gravitation, periodic motion, temperature and heat, thermodynamics.

nodes.title: General Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 22 with a minimum grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Mechanical waves, sound, electric charge and electric field, Gauss Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: General Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 23 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4A.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: General Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 24 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6A.
nodes.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Programming for the Physical Sciences
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Computer Programming
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2B or 3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5

items.text: AP Calculus BC Exam with a score of 5

nodes.description: An introduction to programming and data analysis for the physical sciences. Topics include syntax, goodcoding practice, basic algorithmic structure, plotting, basic data analysis, numerical root-finding and integration.

nodes.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Linear Algebra: Vector spaces, operators, spectral decomposition. Topics may include Sturm-Liouville equations, special functions. Fourier series and Fourier transforms, Dirac delta-function.

nodes.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 5C or 6B with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Analytic functions, contour integrals and branch cuts. Conformal mapping. Laplace transforms. Asymptotic series and the gamma function. Greens functions.

nodes.title: Intermediate Mechanics and Special Relativity
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-. Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Newtonian mechanics in 3D. Conservation laws. Complex numbers. Oscillations. Inertial reference frames, Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum and energy, four-vectors.

nodes.title: Advanced Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 103 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Calculus of variations. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics. Central force problems and collision theory. Non-inertial reference frames. Coupled oscillations and waves.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.
nodes.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

nodes.title: Electromagnetism
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 6B with minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Electrostatics, Laplace's equation, method of images, separation of variables, multipole expansion, magnetostatics, electric and magnetic fields in matter.

nodes.title: Electromagnetism
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 110A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Electrodynamics, Maxwells equations, conservation laws, electromagnetic waves, potentials and fields for moving charges, radiation, special relativity.

nodes.title: Quantum Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 and Physics 100A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: The postulates of quantum mechanics, the Schrdinger equation and its consequences, the quantum harmonic oscillator and other one dimensional quantum systems, Hilbert Space and Dirac notation, the hydrogen atom.

nodes.title: Quantum Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Spin and angular momentum, Clebsch-Gordan coefficients, identical particles, symmetries and conservation laws, time independent perturbation theory.

nodes.title: Quantum Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: The variational principle, time dependent perturbation theory, the adiabatic theorem. Topics from: WKB approximation, the Dirac equation, Berrys phase, Bells inequality, quantum cryptography, quantum computation.

nodes.title: Group Theory for Physicists
nodes.prereq_text: Physics PHYS 110A
nodes.description: The emphasis is on developing some intuition about the role of symmetries in physics, rather than going through rigorous mathematical proofs. Theorems will be proved at the level of rigor customary among physicists.

nodes.title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
nodes.prereq_text: PHYS 22 and MATH 6B with a minimum grade of C-
nodes.description: Principles of statistical physics, entropy, large numbers, thermodynamic principles, microcanonical ensemble, ideal gas, free energy, chemical potential, selected applications. Canonical ensemble, if time permits.

nodes.title: Thermal and Statistical Physics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: SOFT AND LIVING MATTER
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115A and Physics 119A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Canonical ensemble and partition functions, grand canonical ensemble, quantum statistics, Fermi-Dirac, Bose-Einstein distribution laws. Topics from: Brownian motion, Langevin equation, dissipation and fluctuations, elementary kinetic theory, weakly interacting gases or mean field theory of magnetism, other topics illustrative of the breadth of the subject and/or selected applications.

nodes.title: Physics of California Waves, Weather, Quakes and Fires
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25.
nodes.description: Why do the waves hit the beach every five seconds? This course teaches students the relevant fluid dynamics and allows them to apply it to natural phenomena of California: seismic waves, tsunamis, maximum tree heights, fluid flow around fish.

nodes.title: Condensed Matter Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115A with at least a C- or better, and upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Classification of solids; crystal symmetry; thermal, electronic, and magnetic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators; band theory of electronic states; wave scattering by crystals; semiconductor devices.

nodes.title: Condensed Matter Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Tight binding model, topological insulator, magnetism, phase transition, introduction to superconductivity.

nodes.title: Elementary Particle Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 115B.
nodes.description: Introduction to quarks and leptons and the phenomenology of the particles they comprise; fundamental symmetries, invariance principles, and the associated quantum numbers, strong, electromagnetic, and weak interactions and their relationship.

nodes.title: Laboratory Optics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 24 or 7C with a grade of C- or better, Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better
nodes.description: An introduction to optical phenomena and the methods and instrumentation used to generate, measure, and manipulate light. Experiments will cover imaging and aberrations, coherence, diffraction, interference, interferometry, Fourier optics, reflection and polarization, spectroscopy, lasers, fiber optics, and optical instruments.

nodes.title: Analog Electronics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: SOFT AND LIVING MATTER
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 13CL or 20CL and Math 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Passive circuits, diodes, transistors, field effect transistors, operational amplifiers, feedback and control. Design, building and testing of analog circuits.

nodes.title: Digital Electronics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 127AL with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Gates, combinational and sequential logic, ?multiplexers, counters, shift registers, memory and microprocessors. Design, building and testing of digital circuitry, including a modern microprocessor based computer system.

nodes.title: Advanced Experimental Physics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: SOFT AND LIVING MATTER
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 13CL or Physics 20CL or Physics CS 15C. Physics 115A (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Selected experiments in physics, i.e. saturated absorption spectroscopy, muon lifetime measurements, pulsed nuclear magnetic resonance, Mossbauer effect. Develop skills in detailing observations in a scientific notebook, data collection and error analysis, operating complex physical apparatus, and scientific communication.

nodes.title: Introduction to Scientific Computation
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 with a grade of C- or better, and Mathematics 6B with a grade of C- or better; Physics 29 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: A survey of computers, programming, and computational techniques for the natural sciences. Physical foundations of computation, binary arithmetic, computer architecture, programming languages, operating systems, UNIX shell and filesystems. Programming tools, variables and data structures, expressions, control flow, files, functions and scoping, objects, error handling, debugging, graphics, text processing, networking, data acquisition and transfer. Mathematics and algorithms for data processing and analysis, numerical methods, random numbers and simulation.

nodes.title: Gravitation and Relativity
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 103-104 with a minimum grade of C- in each.
nodes.description: An introduction to Einstein's general relativity, the spacetime of special relativity, the principle of equivalence, gravity as geometry, the description of spacetime geometry, the spacetime of a relativistic star, solar system test of general relativity, gravitational collapse, black holes, cosmology.

nodes.title: Stellar Structure and Evolution
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Observed properties and classification of stars, the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, stellar atmospheres, hydrostatic equilibrium, energy transport, equations of state, thermonuclear reaction rates, origin of the elements, life history of stars, stellar death, compact objects, star formation.

nodes.title: Cosmology
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: The geometry, contents and evolution of the universe as a whole. The empirical and theoretical foundations for the Big Bang, the Hubble expansion, Friedmann models, dark matter, dark energy, the thermal history of the universe, the origin of the light elements, the cosmic microwave background, reionization, and structure formation.

nodes.title: Observational Astrophysics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Techniques and implementation of observational methods in astronomy/astrophysics. Sensors, digital-image processing and analysis, research projects with computer-controlled remote access telescope using a digital image sensor. Studies of variable stars, galaxy morphology, supernovae, etc.

nodes.title: Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 6C or 5 or 25.
nodes.description: Structure and function of cellular molecules (lipids, nucleic acids, proteins, and carbohydrates). Genetic engineering techniques of molecular biology. Biomolecular materials and biomedical applications (e.g., bio-sensors, drug delivery systems, gene carrier systems).

nodes.title: Galaxies
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-, Physics 104 (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: The distribution of mass in galaxies, orbits of stars, Boltzmann equation, Jeans theorem, spiral structure & density waves, dynamics of star clusters, galaxy collisions, dynamical friction, gas dynamics, sound & shock waves, gas inflow & accretion, gas outflow & winds.

nodes.title: Planets and Exoplanets
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 5 or 25 or 115A with a minimum grade of C-, Physics 104 (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: An introduction to planets both in and out of the solar system. This course will provide a broad overview of planets in the solar system, the techniques used to detect planets outside the solar system, and demographics and characteristics of exoplanets.

nodes.title: Soft Matter Physics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: SOFT AND LIVING MATTER
nodes.prereq_text: Co-requisite: Physics 119B
nodes.description: A physics-based approach to study the structure, assembly and dynamical properties of a variety of soft materials, such as simple and complex fluids, colloidal systems, liquid crystals, polymers, granular matter and gels, including biological examples. Topics covered include elasticity, viscosity and viscoelasticity, capillarity and wetting, phases and phase diagrams of soft materials, entropy-driven phase transitions, Brownian motion and active matter.

nodes.title: Physical Biology of the Cell
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: SOFT AND LIVING MATTER
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 119B
nodes.description: The role of physics in biology through quantitative measurements and modeling, the organization of a cell, and exemplary quantitative results of biological model systems. The physics of biologically relevant macromolecules, including DNA, RNA and mechanisms of transcription and translation; introduction to protein folding and the role of electrostatics in biology. The physics of the cytoskeleton including beam theory, persistence length, molecular motors, instrumentation used to characterize motor properties, as well as the role of active stresses in cell biology. If time permits, a brief introduction to cell motility and the structure of epithelial tissue.

nodes.title: Optics
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: SOFT AND LIVING MATTER
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 110B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Modern geometrical and physical optics. Polarization, coherence, interference, and diffraction phenomena. Fourier transform spectroscopy, intensity correlation interferometry, spatial filtering, and holography. Selected topics on lasers, light scattering, and quantum optics as time permits.

nodes.title: Science for the Public
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Provides experience in communicating science and technology to nonspecialists. The major components of the course are field work in mentoring, a biweekly seminar, presentations to precollege students and to adult nonscientists, and end-of-term research papers.

nodes.title: Teaching and Learning Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Introduction to basic concepts in education literature and learning theory. The course involves readings of articles and text drawn from general and Physics education research and cognitive science. Students will engage in discussions and reflective activities that apply and relate the ideas from the readings to their own classroom experiences to help them become more effective teachers and learners.

nodes.title: Atomic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: PHYS 115A; concurrent enrollment in PHYS 115B.
nodes.description: An introduction to atomic physics. Covers basic atomic structure of one and two valence electron atoms, the Zeeman effect, and the semiclassical treatment of atoms interacting with near-resonant light. We also discuss laser cooling and trapping, as well as selected advanced topics such as atomic clocks, trapped ion dynamics, and the application of atoms in quantum information science.

nodes.title: Introduction to Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics CS 31; consent of instructor; Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only.

items.text: Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only

nodes.description: Covers the essence of experimental research. Students study three different systems experimentally, and write short Physical Review style articles about the results. Students are responsible for deciding what to measure, how to analyze data, and what conclusions can be reached.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics CS 15A; consent of instructor; Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only.

items.text: Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only

nodes.description: Computer control of experiments. Students learn LabView, and use it to measure and generate analog signals using a data acquisition card and a personal computer. Students ultimately use their computers to measure and control the temperature of a copper rod.

nodes.title: Experimental Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics CS 15B; consent of instructor; Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only.

items.text: Creative Studies and CCS Physics majors only

nodes.description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.

nodes.title: Newtonian Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; creative studies majors only.
nodes.description: Vectors. Kinematics. Newton's laws of motion. Work and energy. Conservativeforces. Momentum. Conservation of momentum. Center of mass motion. Collisions. Systems with variable mass.

nodes.title: Principles of Data Science with R
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Science Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B with a minimum grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Provides a foundation for the practice of data science, with an emphasis on the statistical thinking and computer programming required to collect, prepare, and analyze data. Students will explore and implement the data science life cycle in locally relevant contexts. Using the R programming language, the course focuses on the fundamental skills of data manipulation, exploratory data analysis, and data visualization. A key component of the curriculum is learning to ethically communicate findings and to consider the broader impacts of data-driven decisions.

nodes.title: Probability and Statistics
nodes.prereq_text: Math 3C or Math 4A or Math 4AI or Math 6A or Math 6AI completed with a minimum grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Concepts of probability; random variables; combinatorial probability; discrete and continuous distributions; joint distributions, expected values; moment generating functions; law of large numbers and central limit theorems.
